Our neighbor recommended Rapid Restore. We replaced our entire roof.  Rapid Restore’s quote was lower than others, and they offered great warranties. The sales rep, Michael, also threw in extras such as metal gutter guards and new attic vents.
Michael kept sending contracts missing things he said were included and then, when correcting the error, would leave out other things.  Over a few days, Michael sent over a half-dozen contract versions and I kept catching changes and omissions.
We had a new driveway put in just prior to the roof work. Rapid Restore laid down tarps, and used more tarps to funnel debris into a truck rather than offloading a dumpster onto our driveway. Rapid Restore had a large crew and got the job done in a day. Michael and the project manager, Ryan, were always present.
I wanted to inspect everything when they finished. Claiming insurance reasons, they made me use my ladders to climb onto the roof. Sad that they were willing to follow me up on my ladders without the same consideration of my insurance liability.
Everything was fine except they walked away with 1 gutter extension piece we had at ground level, and a 2nd gutter was moved and was no longer over the outflow tray. I pointed the issues out to Ryan and Michael. They said they would come back to fix the problems. Right or wrong, I paid them in full that day.
The next few days were a problem as I would receive emails, texts, and phone calls from various people representing Rapid Restore, multiple times a day, all asking me to leave social media reviews. When I spoke to them on the phone or replied to the emails, I pointed out the job was not complete.  It was less than a week when they came back and replaced the missing extension and relocated the other downspout.
All good in the end and I would recommend Rapid Restore. Just be careful to ensure the contract has everything in it that was agreed to, and be prepared to get a constant stream of communications requesting you leave reviews.
